artifacts.notes: Extent as the retrieving lane measured it: Complete uncorrected OCR of Migne, Patrologia Latina vol. 142 (Berno of Reichenau and others), whole volume. NO page image of this volume was fetched; every Berno reading here is optical text only. Uncorrected optical recognition: it is a locating and searching layer, not a text of record, and wording quoted from this volume was collated against page images rather than taken from here. This is the only witness to Berno that this run holds: no leaf of the volume was fetched, so nothing quoted from Berno here rises above an uncollated optical reading.
artifacts.rights_basis: The printing reproduced here was published long before 1931 and is in the public domain in the United States: the repository's own rights reading, recorded at guidance/missals.md section 5 against Cornell's public-domain chart current at 1 January 2026, is that a work first published abroad before 1931 is in the public domain with no term running. The Internet Archive's optical character recognition of a public-domain printing is a mechanical transcription that adds no original authorship, is served without a copyright claim asserted over it, and carries none of the host's markup, navigation or apparatus. The bytes are retained here because guidance/sources.md makes retention the project-wide default and none of its three exemptions reaches this file: it may lawfully be republished, it is not restricted, and at 4.06 MB it is at or below the 5.88 MB that is the largest payload this library already retains.

work.author: Berno of Reichenau
work.description: Berno of Reichenau's treatise on the Mass. Chapter VI, read for this run at columns 1065-1072, asks why the compiler of the chant offices provided twenty-three Sundays between the octave of Pentecost and Advent while the arranger of the lections provided a different number -- the mechanism that produces a chant strand and a reading strand running on different schedules.
work.title: Libellus de quibusdam rebus ad Missae officium pertinentibus
